title: CHUYÊN ĐỀ 4 CÁC CẤP SO SÁNH HSA - ĐỀ LUYỆN TẬP SỐ 2
notes: Chưa có đáp án trong dữ liệu nguồn; hệ thống không chấm điểm đề này.

questions.content: The output of the new factory is nowhere near as high as that of the old one.
options: A. The old factory produced significantly more than the new one.
B. The new factory is almost as productive as the old one.
C. The old factory was slightly more productive than the new one.
D. There is no difference in output between the two factories.

questions.content: The current economic crisis is far more severe than any we have experienced in the last decade.
options: A. No crisis in the last decade has been nearly as severe as the current economic one.
B. The current economic crisis is just as severe as those we have seen in the past.
C. Previous crises in the last decade were significantly more severe than the current economic one.
D. The economic crisis we are facing now is the least severe of the last ten years.

questions.content: As the research progressed, the scientists became increasingly optimistic about the potential results.
options: A. The scientists became less optimistic about the potential results as their research continued to progress.
B. The further the research progressed, the more optimistic the scientists became about the potential results.
C. Progressing with the research made the scientists feel much more pessimistic about the potential results.
D. The potential results of the research made the scientists feel increasingly concerned about their progress.

questions.content: This innovative software is by far the most efficient tool for data analysis available today.
options: A. This innovative software is one of the least efficient tools for data analysis available today.
B. This innovative software is slightly more efficient than other data analysis tools available on the market.
C. Other tools for data analysis are just as efficient as this innovative software available today.
D. No other tool for data analysis available today is nearly as efficient as this innovative software.

questions.content: He is not so much a brilliant scholar as he is a dedicated and hardworking teacher.
options: A. He is more of a dedicated and hardworking teacher than he is a brilliant scholar.
B. He is both a brilliant scholar and a dedicated teacher in equal measure and capacity.
C. He is much more of a brilliant scholar than a dedicated and hardworking teacher.
D. He is neither a brilliant scholar nor a dedicated and hardworking teacher in his professional life.

questions.content: I would sooner resign from my position than compromise my professional ethics and integrity.
options: A. I prefer compromising my professional ethics and integrity to resigning from my current position.
B. Resigning from my position is the last thing I would do to protect my professional ethics.
C. I would rather resign from my position than compromise my professional ethics and integrity.
D. My professional ethics and integrity are less important to me than keeping my current position.

questions.content: The renovation of the historic opera house cost twice as much as the initial estimates suggested.
options: A. The opera house renovation cost significantly less than what the initial estimates had originally suggested.
B. The initial estimates for the opera house renovation were only half of the actual total cost.
C. The actual cost of the opera house renovation was exactly the same as the initial estimates.
D. The initial estimates suggested that the renovation of the opera house would be much more expensive.

questions.content: Nowhere is the impact of climate change more evident than in the rapidly melting Arctic ice.
options: A. The impact of climate change is more evident in the rapidly melting Arctic ice than anywhere else.
B. The rapidly melting Arctic ice shows the impact of climate change less than other global regions.
C. Climate change has no evident impact on the Arctic ice compared to other parts of the world.
D. Other regions show the impact of climate change much more clearly than the melting Arctic ice.

questions.content: The more sophisticated the artificial intelligence becomes, the more ethical dilemmas it seems to create.
options: A. The sophistication of artificial intelligence has no direct impact on the number of ethical dilemmas created.
B. Sophisticated artificial intelligence leads to fewer ethical dilemmas than simpler forms of technology.
C. Ethical dilemmas increase in proportion to the level of sophistication of the artificial intelligence.
D. Artificial intelligence becomes less sophisticated as it creates more complex and difficult ethical dilemmas.

questions.content: Her second performance was a far cry from the amateurish display she gave during the auditions.
options: A. Her second performance was significantly better than the amateurish display she gave during the auditions.
B. Her performance during the auditions was much more professional than her second display on stage.
C. There was very little difference between her second performance and the display during the auditions.
D. Her second performance was just as amateurish as the display she gave during the initial auditions.

questions.content: Gasoline prices are nothing like as affordable as they were during the previous summer season.
options: A. Prices for gasoline have remained relatively stable since the end of the previous summer season.
B. Gasoline was more expensive during the previous summer season than it is at the present time.
C. Gasoline prices are much higher now than they were during the previous summer season.
D. It is much more affordable to buy gasoline now than it was during the last summer.

questions.content: Of all the architectural marvels in the city, the cathedral is arguably the most breathtaking.
options: A. No one considers the cathedral to be a breathtaking architectural marvel compared to other buildings.
B. The cathedral is definitely less breathtaking than several other architectural marvels located in the city.
C. Many people believe that the cathedral is the most breathtaking architectural marvel in the city.
D. The cathedral is one of the many architectural marvels that are not very breathtaking at all.

questions.content: The task was not nearly as formidable as the team had originally led us to believe.
options: A. The task was much easier than we had been led to believe by the project team.
B. The team correctly informed us that the task would be extremely formidable and difficult to complete.
C. We found the task to be significantly more formidable than the team had originally described it.
D. The task was exactly as formidable as the team had led us to believe from the start.

questions.content: It is becoming increasingly difficult for young graduates to secure stable employment in this market.
options: A. Young graduates are finding it much easier to secure stable employment in the current job market.
B. Secure employment is getting harder and harder for young graduates to find in the current market.
C. Stable employment has always been difficult for young graduates to secure regardless of the market.
D. The job market is providing more stable employment opportunities for young graduates than ever before.

questions.content: This smartphone model is marginally more expensive than its predecessor, yet it offers better features.
options: A. This smartphone model and its predecessor cost exactly the same despite the difference in features.
B. The previous smartphone model was much more expensive than this current version with better features.
C. There is a huge price difference between this smartphone model and its much cheaper predecessor.
D. This smartphone model costs slightly more than the previous version but has significantly better features.

questions.content: He is easily the most talented violinist that the prestigious conservatory has ever produced.
options: A. There is no doubt that he is the most talented violinist from the prestigious conservatory.
B. He is one of the many talented violinists who have graduated from the prestigious conservatory.
C. Other violinists from the prestigious conservatory are significantly more talented than he has ever been
D. He is less talented than most of the violinists who have studied at the prestigious conservatory.

questions.content: The film was less a romantic comedy than a profound exploration of human isolation.
options: A. The film focused more on exploring human isolation than on being a typical romantic comedy.
B. The film was a very successful romantic comedy that also explored the theme of isolation.
C. Exploration of human isolation was less important to the film than its romantic comedy elements.
D. The film failed to be either a romantic comedy or a profound exploration of human isolation.

questions.content: The consequences of the decision were a great deal more serious than anyone had anticipated.
options: A. Everyone anticipated that the consequences of the decision would be extremely serious and far-reaching.
B. The decision led to consequences that were much more serious than what people had expected.
C. The consequences of the decision were actually less serious than what most people had originally feared.
D. Nobody was surprised by the serious consequences because they had anticipated them from the beginning.

questions.content: Living in the countryside is nowhere near as stressful as living in a bustling metropolis.
options: A. The countryside is just as stressful as a bustling metropolis for those who live there.
B. Living in a bustling metropolis is significantly more stressful than living in the quiet countryside.
C. It is much more stressful to live in the countryside than in a large bustling metropolis.
D. There is no difference in stress levels between living in the countryside and a bustling metropolis.

questions.content: She is getting more and more disillusioned with the political system in her country.
options: A. She has never felt any disillusionment with the political system of her country until quite recently.
B. She is becoming less disillusioned with the political system as she learns more about it.
C. Her level of disillusionment with the political system has remained the same for many years.
D. Her disillusionment with the political system in her country is increasing at a steady rate.

questions.content: This is the least of our problems considering the current state of the company.
options: A. We have many problems that are much more serious than this one given the company's state.
B. This is the most serious problem that the company is currently facing in its entire history.
C. Considering the company's state, we should focus all our attention on solving this particular problem.
D. The company has no other problems except for this very small and insignificant one right now.

questions.content: Few things are as precious as the time we spend with our loved ones.
options: A. Most things are much more precious than the time we spend with our family and friends.
B. The time we spend with our loved ones is one of the most precious things imaginable.
C. Spending time with loved ones is not as precious as many people seem to believe nowadays.
D. Time spent with loved ones is the least precious thing compared to wealth and high status.

questions.content: It is not so much the price as the quality that attracts customers.
options: A. Both the price and the quality are equally important when it comes to attracting loyal customers.
B. The price of the product is much more important than its quality in attracting new customers.
C. Customers are attracted more by the quality of the product than by its actual selling price.
D. Customers do not care about the quality or the price of the products they buy today.

questions.content: This is the very best result we could have hoped for under these conditions.
options: A. We could have achieved a much better result if the conditions had been slightly more favorable.
B. Given the current conditions, it was impossible to achieve a result better than this one today.
C. This result is the worst we could have expected given the conditions we were working under.
D. The conditions were so good that we should have achieved a much better result than this.

questions.content: The more you practice, the more natural the movements will become to you.
options: A. Practicing more will make your movements feel much less natural than they were at the beginning.
B. Your movements will become increasingly natural in proportion to the amount of practice you do daily.
C. The naturalness of your movements has nothing to do with how much you practice every day.
D. You will find that your movements become natural even if you do not practice very often.

questions.content: Living in a small town is nothing like as exciting as living in London.
options: A. London is significantly more exciting than living in a small town could ever be for anyone.
B. Living in a small town is just as exciting as living in a city like London.
C. A small town offers much more excitement than a large and busy city like London does.
D. There is very little difference in excitement between living in a small town and in London.

questions.content: The consequences of ignoring the warning were twice as severe as he had imagined.
options: A. Ignoring the warning led to consequences that were exactly as severe as he had originally imagined.
B. The consequences were much less severe than what he had imagined they would be after ignoring.
C. He correctly imagined how severe the consequences of ignoring the warning would eventually be for him.
D. He had imagined that the consequences of ignoring the warning would be only half as severe.

questions.content: The second edition of the book is a far cry from the original version.
options: A. The second edition of the book is significantly different and much better than the original version.
B. There are very few differences between the second edition and the original version of the book.
C. The original version of the book was much more successful than the second edition published recently.
D. The second edition is just as good as the original version of the book in every way.

questions.content: She is easily the most diligent student I have ever had the pleasure of teaching.
options: A. She is one of the many diligent students that I have taught during my long career.
B. I have never taught a student who was nearly as diligent as she is in class.
C. Teaching her is not as much of a pleasure as teaching other more diligent students here.
D. Some of the students I have taught were much more diligent than she has ever been.

questions.content: The situation is going from bad to worse as the days pass by.
options: A. Each passing day brings a slight improvement to the situation which was originally quite bad indeed.
B. The situation is slowly improving as more time passes and more people get involved in it.
C. Passing time has had no effect on the situation, which remains as bad as it was.
D. The situation is deteriorating more and more with each passing day that goes by right now.

questions.content: It is far easier to criticize a plan than it is to create a better one.
options: A. Creating a better plan is much more difficult than simply criticizing one that already exists today.
B. Criticizing a plan and creating a better one are both equally difficult tasks for most people.
C. It is much easier to create a new plan than to criticize one that is currently existing.
D. Criticizing a plan is not as easy as many people think when compared to creating one.

questions.content: The climate in this region is much the same as it was fifty years ago.
options: A. The climate in this region is significantly different from how it was fifty years in the past.
B. There has been very little change in the climate of this region over the last fifty years.
C. Fifty years ago, the climate in this region was much better than it is at present.
D. The climate has changed more in this region than in any other part of the country.

questions.content: No other candidate was even half as qualified for the position as she was.
options: A. She was the least qualified candidate among all those who applied for the high-level position recently.
B. Other candidates were almost as qualified for the position as she was during the interview process.
C. She was significantly more qualified for the position than any of the other candidates who applied.
D. All the candidates were equally qualified for the position, making the final decision very difficult indeed.

questions.content: The impact of the new law was not nearly as widespread as expected.
options: A. People expected the new law to have a much more limited impact than it actually did.
B. The impact of the new law was exactly as widespread as the government had initially predicted.
C. The new law had a much more limited impact than what people had originally expected.
D. The new law was extremely widespread and its impact was much greater than anyone had anticipated.

questions.content: He is arguably the most influential philosopher of the twenty-first century so far.
options: A. He is definitely less influential than other philosophers who have emerged in the twenty-first century recently.
B. Many people consider him to be the most influential philosopher of the twenty-first century until now.
C. There is no doubt that he is the least influential philosopher of the current twenty-first century.
D. He is just one of many philosophers who have had no influence in the twenty-first century.

questions.content: The quality of the new prototype is vastly superior to that of the previous versions.
options: A. The new prototype is nowhere near as good as the earlier models.
B. The previous versions were much better than the new prototype.
C. The new prototype is significantly better than any of the older versions.
D. There is almost no difference in quality between the new and old prototype

questions.content: The cost of the project has been marginally lower than the initial budget allocated.
options: A. The project cost slightly less than the amount of money that was initially allocated in budget.
B. The initial budget was significantly lower than the actual cost of the project upon its completion.
C. There was a substantial difference between the project cost and the initial budget that was allocated.
D. The project cost and the initial budget were exactly the same with no difference at all.

questions.content: Nothing is quite so refreshing as a cold swim on a hot summer afternoon.
options: A. A cold swim on a hot summer afternoon is not as refreshing as people often claim.
B. Many things are much more refreshing than a cold swim during a hot summer afternoon today.
C. A cold swim is the most refreshing thing one can do on a hot summer afternoon.
D. There are few things that are less refreshing than taking a cold swim in the summer.

questions.content: Success in this field is less about luck than it is about persistent hard work.
options: A. Persistent hard work is more important for success in this field than luck could ever be.
B. Luck plays a much more significant role in achieving success in this field than hard work.
C. Both luck and persistent hard work are equally necessary to achieve success in this particular field.
D. Hard work is not as essential as luck when it comes to being successful in this field.

questions.content: The performance was a great deal better than the critics had led us to anticipate.
options: A. We anticipated a much better performance than what was actually delivered according to the critics' reviews.
B. The critics were correct in their anticipation that the performance would be of very high quality.
C. The performance was much worse than what the critics had led us to expect in reviews.
D. The performance exceeded the expectations that the critics had created for us before the show started.

questions.content: The efficiency of the new engine is a far cry from what the developers originally promised.
options: A. There is very little difference between the engine’s current efficiency and the developers’ initial promises.
B. The developers delivered an engine that was exactly as efficient as they had originally promised us.
C. The efficiency of the new engine actually exceeded the original promises made by the development team.
D. The new engine is significantly less efficient than the developers had initially led everyone to believe.

questions.content: The impact of the pandemic on the tourism industry was by far more devastating than anticipated.
options: A. The tourism industry suffered much more devastating effects from the pandemic than anyone had initially expected.
B. People correctly predicted that the pandemic would have a very devastating impact on the tourism industry.
C. The pandemic’s impact on the tourism industry was actually less devastating than what was originally feared.
D. Everyone was surprised that the tourism industry remained relatively unaffected by the global pandemic this year.

questions.content: The latest smartphone model is arguably the most sophisticated piece of technology on the market.
options: A. No one considers the latest smartphone model to be sophisticated when compared to other available devices.
B. The latest smartphone model is definitely less sophisticated than other pieces of technology currently on sale.
C. Many experts believe that the latest smartphone model is the most sophisticated technology available today.
D. The market features many pieces of technology that are significantly more sophisticated than this smartphone model.

questions.content: Her contribution to the charitable foundation was twice as generous as that of the other donors.
options: A. The other donors contributed only half as much money to the charitable foundation as she did.
B. She gave much less money to the charitable foundation than the other donors who were involved.
C. All the donors made equally generous contributions to the charitable foundation during the recent gala event.
D. The other donors were twice as generous as she was when contributing to the charitable foundation.

questions.content: The task of restructuring the entire department was not nearly as simple as it appeared.
options: A. It was a very simple task to restructure the entire department just as we had expected.
B. Restructuring the department proved to be much more complex than it had initially seemed to be.
C. The department restructuring was exactly as simple as everyone had originally thought it would be.
D. We were surprised that restructuring the entire department was even simpler than it appeared at first.

questions.content: I would sooner undergo a difficult surgery than live with this chronic pain for another year.
options: A. Undergoing a difficult surgery is just as unpleasant as living with this chronic pain every day.
B. Living with chronic pain for another year is preferable to me than undergoing a difficult surgery.
C. I would rather endure the chronic pain for another year than have to undergo any surgery.
D. I prefer undergoing a difficult surgery to living with this chronic pain for one more year.

questions.content: The growth of the tech sector has been marginally faster than that of the manufacturing sector.
options: A. Both the tech and the manufacturing sectors have grown at exactly the same rate this year.
B. The manufacturing sector has experienced significantly faster growth than the tech sector in recent times.
C. There is a substantial difference in the growth rates of the tech and the manufacturing sectors.
D. The tech sector has grown only slightly faster than the manufacturing sector during the last few years.

questions.content: Of all the candidates interviewed, she was easily the most articulate and well-prepared for it.
options: A. Other candidates were significantly more articulate and well-prepared than she was during the interview process.
B. She was one of the many candidates who were articulate and well-prepared for the job interview.
C. Without a doubt, she was the most articulate and well-prepared candidate among all those we interviewed.
D. She was less articulate and well-prepared than most of the other candidates who were interviewed today.

questions.content: This investment opportunity is by far the most lucrative one we have seen this decade.
options: A. Other investment opportunities we have seen this decade are just as lucrative as this one today.
B. This investment opportunity is slightly more lucrative than others we have seen during the last decade.
C. No other investment opportunity this decade has been nearly as lucrative as this particular one here.
D. This is one of the least lucrative investment opportunities that we have encountered in ten years.

questions.content: The quality of her latest work is superior to anything she has produced in the past.
options: A. Her latest work is much better than any of the work she has produced previously in her career.
B. All of her previous works are of much higher quality than her most recent latest production.
C. Her latest work is of the same quality as the work she has produced in the past.
D. She has produced many works in the past that are superior to her latest one today
